title: A man lay bleeding on the side of the road.
paragraphs: A man lay bleeding on the side of the road.
And two religious men walked past him.

Maybe they were busy.
Maybe they were afraid.
Maybe they convinced themselves someone else would help.
To the people listening to Jesus, this was the twist.
They were the people good Jews avoided.
He didn’t ask if the man believed the same things he did.
He didn’t check if the man deserved help.
And Jesus ends the story with a question.
“Which of these three was a neighbor?”
This parable exposes something uncomfortable about human nature:
It is possible to know Scripture…
It is possible to hold religious titles…
and miss the heart of God.
Because real faith does not only live in sermons.
Three truths echo from this story:
Mercy reveals the true condition of the heart.
Faith that ignores suffering is incomplete faith.
Sometimes the most godly moment in your day is when you stop for someone else's pain.
And that means the real test of faith may not happen in church.
It may happen on the road…
When was the last time compassion interrupted your schedule—and you chose to stop?
